flagged.title: Chapters 5-8: The Unravelling
flagged.reason: F16 is mark-affecting because it misattributes Poole's direct observations to an invented maid/servant and confuses Poole's sighting of the masked dwarf with Jekyll waking to find his own hairy hand in Chapter 10, which will cause students to lose AO1 textual accuracy marks.

mark_affecting.quote: A glimpsed hand is dwarfish and hairy. A servant saw a creature crying out like a rat.

flagged.title: Chapters 9-10: The Revelations
flagged.reason: At 07:50 the video states that Stevenson called the book 'a fable', which teaches a false fact that will cause students to be marked wrong on the lesson flashcard testing Stevenson's self-description ('a fine bogey tale').

mark_affecting.quote: Stevenson himself called his book a fable

flagged.title: Character Analysis
flagged.reason: The video presents an inaccurate, conflated quotation ('lean, cold, scanty, and yet somehow lovable') both spoken and on screen rather than the correct text ('lean, long, dusty, dreary and yet somehow lovable').

mark_affecting.quote: The book describes him as lean, cold, scanty, and yet somehow lovable.
